solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fondler touring with American musical show

indicators.note: a tour goes all the way round a place, so the first word wraps around the next

blocks.note: someone who fondles is a groper
with and and both mean together with
A is the standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A lecherous man goes on tour with an American stage musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fondler' looks like anagram fodder, but its letters do not fit; it is a synonym for a sex pest.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand opera is a large-scale staged work set entirely to music, so it is a musical show.

clue.text: Boot that is needed after flood?

indicators.note: needed after says the abbreviation is placed behind the other word

blocks.note: to flood out is to well up or gush
i.e. is the abbreviation of Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone recommends the right footwear for wading out after a flood.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the boot pictured is exactly what a flood calls for, though the flood is really a verb meaning gush.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellie is the British short name for a Wellington, a rubber waterproof knee-length piece of footwear.

clue.text: Black inside, nasty old wheat in lethal buffet

indicators.note: nasty suggests something gone bad and twisted, so the following words are rearranged
inside places the abbreviation within the rearranged letters

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A farmer finds stale, blackened grain inside a deadly batch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' here is not a meal but a blow, the sense of being buffeted by wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffet is a blow, so a lethal one is a killing stroke, the final fatal blow.

clue.text: Duke, Russian who was terrible in bed?

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
Ivan the Terrible was the first Tsar of Russia

explanation.surface: A gossipy hint that a Russian duke was a poor performer in the bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible in bed' reads as a slur; the terrible belongs to Ivan's title and bed is a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A divan is a low base-style couch or sofa used for sleeping, a kind of bed.

clue.text: Telephone first love — beautiful nymph

blocks.note: to telephone someone is to call them
1st written out as I ST, with I for one
love is zero in tennis, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A smitten admirer phones their first sweetheart, a lovely nymph.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Callisto was a lovely nymph of Artemis whom Zeus seduced and who became the Great Bear.

clue.text: P-personage travelling north for city on Rhine

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: a personage is a nob, and the stammered P-p tells us to stammer the synonym too, giving N-nob

explanation.surface: Some stuttering dignitary heads north on a trip to a Rhineland city.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in 'P-personage' is copied onto its synonym: NOB becomes N-NOB, which read upwards spells BONN.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonn, former West German capital, stands on the banks of the Rhine river.

clue.text: ‘Second fiddle’ in fiendishly difficult crossword?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
to fiddle with something is to tinker

explanation.surface: Playing second fiddle sounds like a role mentioned inside a very hard puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second fiddle' looks like a fixed phrase for a junior role, but splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinker is informal British slang for something very hard or nasty, like a brutal puzzle.

clue.text: Amusing work from coxed pair?

blocks.note: surface reading: some funny job done by a rowing crew
setter's reading: a coxed pair is two rowers plus a cox, a trio afloat, and the comic book takes its title from such a group

explanation.walkthrough: A coxed pair is a racing boat holding two oarsmen and a cox. Jerome K. Jerome's comic 1889 novel follows three friends on a Thames boating trip.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is a famous humorous Victorian travel book, an amusing literary work about a rowing holiday.

clue.text: Vagrants pee in public transport vehicles

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation within the vehicles word

blocks.note: trams are vehicles running on rails in the streets for public transport
the letter P is pronounced pee

explanation.surface: Rough sleepers relieve themselves on buses and trams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pee' is just how the letter P is said; the clue's crude picture is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramps are homeless wanderers with no fixed home, which is what vagrants are.

clue.text: Ring to cancel engagement on vacation

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied out, so only the outside letters stay

blocks.note: to annul is to cancel or make void
the first and last letters of engagement

explanation.surface: Someone phones to call off a wedding while away on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: An annulet is a small ring, especially a ringed moulding on a column or a ring in heraldry.

clue.text: £9 sent back for Bolshevik

indicators.note: sent back means returned the way it came, so read the letters in reverse

blocks.note: said aloud, nine pounds, with L the sign for pound sterling

explanation.surface: Nine pounds is returned in exchange for a Russian revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: £ is the pound sign, L from Latin libra, so £9 is written out as NINE L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenin led the Bolshevik party in the 1917 October Revolution and founded the Soviet state.

clue.text: Heroin around periodically in or near Asian city

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so take every other letter
turned around means facing the other way, so read backwards

blocks.note: H is slang for heroin
the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of in or near

explanation.surface: Drugs are found periodically in or around an Asian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In or near' looks like a positional phrase about the city, but it is the raw material for the letter picking.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam in Southeast Asia, a major Asian city.

clue.text: Restrain dog with lead, or let sleeping dogs lie?

indicators.note: to restrain something is to hold it in, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for the metal lead
Rover is a traditional name for a dog

explanation.surface: Advice on controlling a dog with a lead, or else leaving it alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' wants to be a leash; it is the metal, whose symbol Pb holds Rover.
explanation.definitionFit: Let sleeping dogs lie is a well-known saying, a short traditional piece of wisdom; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Wind in southern plain daughters must leave

indicators.note: must leave means go away, so this letter is dropped

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
plain, as in unadorned, is naked
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A wind blows across a southern plain from which the farmer's daughters must leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Wind is a verb here, rhyming with kind, not the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: To snake is to follow a twisting, bending path, which is how a road or river can wind.

clue.text: Really good caddie perhaps one in black suit

blocks.note: first meaning: an ace, a star, whose job is all about golf clubs
second meaning: a playing card, the single pip of the black suit

explanation.surface: An excellent golf caddie wears a dark outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: A caddie carries a golfer's clubs, so an ace caddie is cryptically an ace of clubs; one is the ace's value in cards.
explanation.definitionFit: In a deck of playing cards, the single-pip card of the clubs suit, which is black, carries that name.

clue.text: Upset about Gunners increased dramatically

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the second

blocks.note: to upset a drink is to spill it
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: Arsenal, the Gunners, had a sharp rise in fortunes despite something being upset about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gunners' suggests Arsenal football club, nicknamed the Gunners, but here means the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices that spiral rise ever faster, so spiralled means rose steeply and quickly out of control.

clue.text: Changes M&S trousers for partner returning stockings

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so read the words backwards
to trouser is to pocket, so the shop letters take in everything else

blocks.note: M&S is Marks & Spencer, the British department store
pro means for, in favour of
a mate is a partner
hose is an old name for stockings

explanation.surface: A British department store swaps its trouser line for stockings from a partner firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' looks like clothing on sale but is a verb meaning pockets, with M&S wrapped round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Metamorphoses are transformations from one form into another, so the plural noun means changes.

clue.text: Drunk bathes in booze

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering about in disorder, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunkard lies soaking in alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green wormwood-flavoured spirit, a kind of hard liquor.

clue.text: FBI agents sent into Hell — it could be red

indicators.note: sent into means put inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the pit is a name for hell
G-men is American slang for FBI agents, government men

explanation.surface: Federal agents are dispatched into hell, and someone notes the place could be red.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'red' of hellfire is a decoy; the definition is any colouring matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigment is a colouring substance, and red is one example of the colours such material provides.

clue.text: Food store in which ferret keeps insect

indicators.note: keeps means holds onto, so the first word encloses the second

blocks.note: to ferret about is to pry
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A ferret in a larder holds on to a bug it has caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ferret' looks like the animal, but it is the verb meaning to search nosily.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry is a small room or cupboard in a house for keeping provisions.

clue.text: Faith leaders in bed wear, but not judges

indicators.note: but not says leave something out, so these letters are taken away

blocks.note: jim-jams is British informal slang for pyjamas
J is the abbreviation for judge, so two of them

explanation.surface: Religious leaders are seen in their nightclothes, though the judges are not.
explanation.definitionFit: Imams lead prayers in a mosque, so they are Muslim religious leaders.

clue.text: Fruity cordial administered initially if a sailor returns

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take just the opening letter
returns means comes back, so the whole string is read backwards

blocks.note: the opening letter of administered
taken as written
taken as written
a tar is an old name for a sailor

explanation.surface: A fruit drink is given out first when a sailor comes home.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratafia is a sweet liqueur flavoured with almonds or fruit kernels, a fruit-based cordial.

clue.text: Old woman in NATO trained one and all

indicators.note: trained means drilled into new shape, so the letters are rearranged
in places the first piece within the rearranged letters

blocks.note: an old woman is informal for one's mother, ma
taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly woman serving in the military alliance was drilled with the rest of the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To a man is an idiom meaning without exception, everyone together, just as one and all does.

clue.text: Sky god right to replace second one in populous nation

indicators.note: to replace means take the place of, so one letter is swapped for another

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
one is the Roman numeral I, and the second such letter is the one swapped
India is the world's most populous country

explanation.surface: A god of the heavens takes a crowded country's place by right.
explanation.walkthrough: INDIA has two letter Is; swapping R for the second gives INDRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Indra is the Hindu deity of the heavens, lightning, rain and thunder, king of the Vedic gods.

clue.text: Poet finished penning note

indicators.note: penning means enclosing as in a pen, so the first word wraps around

blocks.note: finished is done
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A poet has completed writing a short message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penning' looks like writing, fitting a poet, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: John Donne was the English metaphysical writer of verse and sermons of the early seventeenth century.

clue.text: Month needed with an early South American

definitions.note: the Maya were in fact Central American

blocks.note: May is a month
taken as written

explanation.surface: A month is required to accompany an early traveller in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mayan was a member of the ancient civilisation of Mesoamerica, an early native people.

clue.text: Story that can be spun out?

blocks.note: first meaning: a long tale, often an embellished one
second meaning: thread made by spinning fibre

explanation.walkthrough: Spinning a long tale and spinning wool share a verb; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a rambling tale and spun fibre used in knitting and weaving.

clue.text: Flotilla on river dropping an English handout

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so a letter is removed
in an across clue, one thing on another sits after it, so the first word goes second

blocks.note: the Lea is a river in London and Hertfordshire
a flotilla is a small fleet
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Boats on a river drop English leaflets to the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The river Lea runs through east London into the Thames; only one of the two Es in the fleet goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a printed sheet distributed free, a handout.

clue.text: Novel, novel by A. Bronte, describing hot temper

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new and different, so the letters are rearranged
describing means drawing around, so the rearranged letters enclose the rest

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
temper and anger both mean rage

explanation.surface: A new novel by Anne Bronte describes a fiery temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The book is actually by Jane Austen, not Anne Bronte; the second 'novel' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Northanger Abbey is Jane Austen's Gothic parody, published in 1817, a celebrated English novel.
